input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 (the first of two paragraphs numbered 2.2) imposes full-term exclusive dealing on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no product-category limit, no time limit, and no performance-based exit — the playbook walk-away position. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. We therefore delete the clause to reach the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer), noting the 12-month, category-limited, SLA-terminable fallback if exclusivity is commercially necessary. No other exclusivity language binds Customer; remaining "exclusive" references relate to remedies and jurisdiction.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment in Section 2.2: our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on Customer, and this clause contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. If exclusivity is commercially essential, we could consider a fallback limited to hosted analytics services for 12 months, terminating automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.
proposal.summary: Delete Vendor's sole and exclusive provider status (Section 2.2)
